advantages in 10 cases, with the remaining 60 cases showing
comparable performance within measurement variance.

by 1.2%, with maximum observed savings of 8 MB on hard
problems. Importantly, in some cases, MARCO’s optimizations slightly increased memory usage (by up to 1.9%) to
achieve runtime speedups, highlighting the deliberate tradeoffs between time and space optimizations that characterize
effective HPC code.

We compared memory usage between MARCO-optimized
and baseline LLM-generated code using peak memory consumption metrics recorded with Python’s tracemalloc
module and psutil. Among the 85 evaluated problems (75
easy/medium, 10 hard), MARCO showed measurable memory
usage improvements in 15 cases, while baseline LLMs showed
advantages in 10 cases, with the remaining 60 cases showing
comparable performance within measurement variance.
On average, MARCO reduced peak memory consumption
by 1.2%, with maximum observed savings of 8 MB on hard
problems. Importantly, in some cases, MARCO’s optimizations slightly increased memory usage (by up to 1.9%) to
achieve runtime speedups, highlighting the deliberate tradeoffs between time and space optimizations that characterize
effective HPC code.
